t: KV62 is smaller and less decorated than other royal tombs of its time and probably began as a tomb for a non-royal person, so its 5,398 objects had to be packed densely into the space.
Robbers entered twice within a few years of the burial, but the tomb was resealed and then buried under debris, so Tutankhamun's mummy and most of the goods stayed intact.
Howard Carter and Lord Carnarvon found it in 1922; the clearance took ten digging seasons, and most of the contents went to the Egyptian Museum in Cairo rather than being divided with the sponsors.
dyk: Among the furniture was a foldable bed, the only intact example known from ancient Egypt, and a reed staff labelled as one that the king "cut with his own hand".
ev: Tutankhamun was buried in KV62, which was robbed twice within a few years and resealed each time
Howard Carter's excavators found the first step of the entrance staircase and reached the antechamber on 26 November
The excavators opened the coffins and removed the mummy, and a legal dispute with the Egyptian government over access ended
The last shipment of conserved burial goods was sent to Cairo
A theft from the sarcophagus after 1926 came to light when the anatomist Ronald Harrison re-examined the remains
A rainstorm flooded the tomb through a fault in the burial chamber ceiling
The mummy was moved to a climate-controlled glass display case in the antechamber
A renovation of the tomb, begun with the Getty Conservation Institute in 2009, was completed

f.made: Commissioned for Tutankhamun, an Eighteenth Dynasty pharaoh who reigned c. 1332–1323 BCE; probably begun as a non-royal tomb, possibly intended for his advisor Ay, and enlarged after the king's premature death
f.form: A rock-cut tomb of four chambers (antechamber, annexe, burial chamber and treasury) with an entrance staircase of sixteen steps and a corridor 8 metres long; painted decoration only in the burial chamber
f.where: In the eastern branch of the Valley of the Kings, cut into the valley floor; the mummy and sarcophagus remain in the tomb, most of the goods were sent to Cairo and have been moving to the Grand Egyptian Museum in Giza
f.known: a complete set of royal burial goods; the golden funerary mask; the gilded shrines and nested coffins; the discovery of 1922 by Howard Carter; the media frenzy called Tutmania; the rumoured curse; evidence of ancient tomb robbery
